business_problem: The U.S. Navy needs to process very large volumes of combat-system data quickly enough to improve situational awareness, detect and identify emerging threats, and reduce operator reaction time, including against hypersonic threats.
solution_summary: Lockheed Martin describes an in-house AI and machine learning implementation inside the Aegis environment for the U.S. Navy. Naval radars generate high volumes of electronic-signature and other operational data that feed the Aegis Fire Control system, where AI methods and AI algorithms are used to autonomously recognize patterns subtler than conventional software decision aids can detect. Those results are surfaced through the broader Aegis Combat System to improve situational awareness, operator decision support, and reaction time against fast-moving threats, including hypersonic targets. The company also applies AI across Aegis lifecycles, using operational and engineering data for predictive maintenance and pairing AI with model-based engineering processes to identify hardware and software issues earlier, reduce cost, and deliver new capability builds faster. Lockheed Martin says deployment is controlled through design, test, and review artifacts aligned to Department of Defense AI Ethical Principles and reviewed with customer stakeholders before release.

solution_components.name: Naval radars
solution_components.role: Generate the sensor and electronic-signature data that AI methods analyze for threat detection.

solution_components.name: Aegis Fire Control system
solution_components.role: Processes complex combat data and applies AI methods to detect, track, and identify emerging threats.

solution_components.name: Aegis Combat System
solution_components.role: Delivers AI-enabled situational awareness and decision support to operators and commanders across Aegis lifecycles.

data_flow: Sensor and electronic-signature data from naval radars flows into the Aegis Fire Control system, where AI methods analyze patterns in the data to improve detection, tracking, and identification of threats. The outputs are then presented through the Aegis Combat System to support operators and commanders, while additional operational and engineering data is used for predictive maintenance and earlier hardware/software issue identification.
business_outcome: The AI-enhanced Aegis implementation is intended to improve situational awareness, operator decision making, and reaction time; improve detection, tracking, and identification of emerging threats; maximize uptime through predictive maintenance; and reduce cost while delivering new capability builds faster.
architecture_clues: AI is being developed and fielded across Aegis Combat System lifecycles from the factory to the fleet.
The Aegis Combat System is described as combining over 50 years of continuous evolution.
The team includes hundreds of AI and Machine Learning engineers.
The ethical and deployment process is aligned to the five Department of Defense AI Ethical Principles: Responsible, Equitable, Traceable, Reliable and Governable.
The system is described as needing to defend against hypersonic threats flying more than five times the speed of sound.
